title: Harder targets: money to reach them, 5 runs per setup, $0.40 a lab (Nov 9)

design.question: For the same agents and checker, how much money does each way of organizing the labs spend to reach the same number of targets?
design.compare: OSO, α 0.2, Shared library, Planner with a good strategy, Plain planner, Pay per lemma, Traditional
design.fixed: the same 4 agents (the single agent: the first, with all the money), $1.60 in all, Lean checks every proof
design.measure: median money, all labs together, to reach 7 of the 11 targets; 7 is the highest count that more than half the runs of every setup reached; a run that never got there counts as not reached

answer: Median money, all labs together, to reach 7 of the 11 targets: OSO, α 0.2 $0.727; Shared library $0.509; Planner with a good strategy $0.203; Plain planner $1.137; Pay per lemma $0.699; Traditional $0.812. OSO, α 0.2 minus Shared library: +$0.218. OSO, α 0.2 minus Planner with a good strategy: +$0.524. OSO, α 0.2 minus Plain planner: −$0.410. OSO, α 0.2 minus Pay per lemma: +$0.028. OSO, α 0.2 minus Traditional: −$0.085.

caveats: Labs could not stop early: each worked until its money or the rounds ran out, so setups are compared at the same money spent.

Rewards differ from the current simulation model: the knowledge reward is off (the simulation pays 1 per new bit since v5): Lean has no agreed measure of a result's new knowledge yet, see docs/design.md; value flowing back is split by the lines each parent saves (its own proof's length in symbols), a stand-in for the work it saves (1/p) in the simulation.

Money to a count is all labs together, to the end of the round that reached it. Medians have ranges of at least 95% from the sorted runs; differences of medians have 95% ranges from resampling the runs; runs are not paired. Other table values are mean ± standard deviation.

Planner with a good strategy has advantages the other setups lack: its prompt says how to split the work, and it sees what each lab tried last round and why it failed. A win for it may come from these hints rather than from coordination. Lab 1 only plans, so three labs prove and most of its money stays unspent.
The plain planner has the same information as the labs (no strategy advice, no failure reports). Lab 1 only plans, so three labs prove.
